newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 30.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
TELECOMMUNICATION, POSTAL STRIKE ENDS

A nationwide postal and telecommunication employees strike was called off following acceptance of their demands. The decision, seven days after the strike started, left a massive backlog in postal services and crippled telecommunications across the country. Analyst estimate a cumulative 10 billion rupee loss due to the week-long strike.
The Hindustan Times
FORMER PREMIER STANDS TRIAL IN SPECIAL COURT

Former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao will appear before a special trial court in New Delhi hearing the St. Kitts forgery case. Following a Supreme Court order, all arrangements have been made to provide Rao with maximum security cover. Rao is the first former premier to appear in court on charges of conspiracy and cheating.
The Economic Times
BOURSE REGULATOR STEPS IN TO LIFT SAGGING MARKETS

The bourse regulator (SEBI) has finalised steps to boost sagging stock markets. The measures include further expansion of the Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) online trading system (BOLT) and a reduction in the size of minimum applications. The steps are likely to boost the debt markets and facilitate institutionalisation of the market system with flexible and hands-off regulation for mutual funds and venture funds. The BOLT scheme approved by the SEBI will allow BSE as well as stockbrokers of other bourses to set up in cities where there are no regional bourses and through memoranda of understanding with the respective bourses in the same cities.
FISCAL DEFICIT ON TARGET, REVENUE DEFICIT LOWER

Finance Minister P Chidambaram said the fiscal deficit would be kept on target at five percent of gross domestic product. Reaffirming government's attempts to maintain fiscal discipline, he said it had achieved a lower revenue deficit than in the previous five fiscal years. On making labour laws flexible, Chidambaram said the government had yet to take a decision.
FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS SHELVE ECB PLANS

Term lending financial institutions (FIs) are understood to have shelved external commercial borrowing (ECB) plans for the timebeing. According to sources, the FIs were likely to scrap their ECB plans for 1996 if logistics did not work out in their favour. The FIs are said to be awaiting the central bank's (RBI's) future guidelines and the likely reaction of corporates to it. If corporates opted for a foreign exchange loan from a bank, there would be no need to go for ECB, said sources. This was allowed in the RBI's recent monetary policy announcement under which banks were permitted to lend their FCNR (B) funds in the domestic market.
Financial Express
CLEARANCE FOR REVAMPED MUTUAL FUNDS GUIDELINES

The revamped Mutual Fund regulations were cleared by the stock market regulator (SEBI). The existing fee structure for Asset Management Companies (AMCs) was retained. The borrowing facility by the mutual fund was extended to include dividend and interest payments. SEBI retraced its earlier decision to link the fee charged by an AMC to the performance of the scheme. It was decided to retain the present fee structure of 1.25 percent NAV of weekly average net assets for corpus upto one billion rupees and one percent for that above 20 million rupees.
PRIVATE PARTIES MAY BE ALLOWED IN POWER DISTRIBUTION

The government is considering changes in the Electricity Act to allow private sector participation in the transmission and distribution sectors. Other planned steps include divesting the Central Electricity Authority (CEA) of its powers to review any renovation and maintenance projects. The government plans to scrap the clause that makes CEA approval mandatory from the new Electricity Act. The bill to amend the Act is likely to be passed in the winter session of the Parliament.
ACTIVE PRIVATE ROLE IN CORE SECTOR SOUGHT

The action plan on infrastructure (1997-2006) adopted at the UN-ESCAP ministerial conference in New Delhi called for active involvement of the private sector. It emphasised the need for greater transparency to improve the infrastructure sector in the region. The action plan called for preparation of a Green Paper on telecommunication problems. The ESCAP Secretariat has been asked to undertake a study for implementing the railway project connecting Central Asia with Southeast Asia.
GRIDCO, AES SIGN FRESH AGREEMENT

State-owned transmission and distribution firm GRIDCO and U.S. utility company AES Transpower signed a fresh power purchase agreement (PPA) for the entire upgraded 500 mw lb valley coal fired thermal power project. The PPA incorporates the revised terms and conditions renegotiated after the new state government came into power in 1995.
Business Standard
RELIANCE SIGNS CHEAPEST GSM DEAL

Reliance group company, Reliance Telecom, has concluded a $105 million deal with Motorola to set up its cellular network in the seven circles for which it holds licences. Motorola has the entire project on a turnkey basis. It will design and set up the radio network in addition to sourcing GSM exchanges. It is understood that Motorola has also struck a $25 million deal with Ericsson for supplying seven 50,000 line exchanges.
DEADLINE TO TABLE COMPANIES BILL DRAFT EXTENDED

The Department of Company Affairs (DCA) has advanced the deadline for submission of a draft report by the working group on the companies bill. The committee will have to submit its report by November 30, a month ahead of the deadline set by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram. The deadline has been changed to ensure the submission of report to the government on time. There are, however, indications that the working group will be unable to meet the new deadline.
USE OF NAPHTHA BY POWER UNITS CLEARED

The committee of secretaries has decided to allocate naphtha to all power plants, being set up in environmentally sensitive areas. The panel also decided that naphtha might be imported, if necessary. Meanwhile, the Indian Oil Corporation, the canalising agency for naphtha imports, has floated a tender in Singapore to buy 60,000 tonnes of naphtha. This would be the first instalment of imported naphtha for power utilities.
